quest.ship_voyage.title: A Voyage on the Polden
quest.ship_voyage.desc: Two days at sea: six islands, two dinners, one captain's waltz. The shore comes back on Sunday evening.
quest.ship_voyage.done: I'm ashore. The pier is swaying, though it's me. Two days, six islands and a couple of dozen people who weren't in my life on Friday. The ship moves out to the roads and puts her lights on. On Friday she takes passengers again.
quest.ship_voyage.fri.log: I'm aboard. The motor ship Polden, a yellow disc on her funnel. We sailed at six: three blasts, a march from the loudspeaker, and the town went flat as a postcard. The Stone Brothers at sunset, then dinner and a concert. The programme hangs by the purser's desk. I don't know anyone here.
quest.ship_voyage.first_night.obj: Live through the first evening and night aboard
quest.ship_voyage.sat.log: Saturday. I woke because the floor was humming: the diesel, you get used to it like your own pulse. Bird Island at ten, the Far Light after tea, and they say we can go ashore there, the captain's dinner and dancing tonight. Yesterday's strangers nod to me at breakfast as if I were one of them.
quest.ship_voyage.saturday.obj: Live through Saturday: Bird Island, the deck games, the Far Light
quest.ship_voyage.eve.log: Saturday evening. The captain's dinner: white tablecloths, Gromov in his dress tunic gives a toast of eleven words. Then the quartet, a waltz, the saloon windows reflected in black water. At midnight we anchor off Long Island, and the diesel falls silent for the first time since Friday.
quest.ship_voyage.second_night.obj: Live through the captain's evening and the night at anchor
quest.ship_voyage.sun.log: Sunday. We lay at anchor off Long Island all night, so quiet you could hear Aunt Pasha put the kettle on in the galley. Today the quiz, the Seal Rocks, diplomas at three, and at six our own roads. Everyone already says "here on the Polden". So do I.
quest.ship_voyage.sunday.obj: Live through Sunday: the quiz, the Seal Rocks, the diplomas at three
quest.ship_voyage.home.log: The diplomas have been given out. The suitcases already stand in the corridors, and still nobody leaves the deck. At half past four our lighthouse will show ahead, at six the roads. Everyone is writing addresses for everyone else on napkins from the buffet.
quest.ship_voyage.come_home.obj: Reach the roads of Lyudmilovsk and go ashore
quest.ship_cat.title: The Stowaway in the Hold
quest.ship_cat.desc: Zoya the stewardess hears someone crying under the cargo hatch at night. The bosun must not find out.
quest.ship_cat.done: The Polden has a secret that everyone keeps from everyone else: Bosun the cat and three kittens in the hold. The bosun brings her sour cream, Zoya brings sausages, Aunt Pasha counts her fish. Now I keep the secret too. It's a good one.
quest.ship_cat.hear.log: Zoya the stewardess carries the tea and studies the economics of sea transport by correspondence. She says someone cries under the hatch on the foredeck at night. She is at the dining room's serving hatch at meals, and between breakfast and dinner there or in the cabins.
quest.ship_cat.listen.log: The cargo hatch is on the foredeck, by the windlass. Zoya won't go there alone. Not a word to Taras the bosun: he allows no animals aboard, there was some business with a goat. Listen at the hatch. It carries better at night.
quest.ship_cat.hear_hatch.obj: Listen at the cargo hatch on the foredeck
quest.ship_cat.milk.log: Something lives under the hatch. By day it is dull as a barrel down there, but at night there is meowing, and in more than one voice. By the coaming lies a fish tail picked clean: gulls don't eat like that. Nobody is crying. It's a cat, and a cat needs milk. The dining room's buffet hatch sells milk in three-cornered cartons, from seven in the morning till nine at night.
quest.ship_cat.get_milk.obj: Buy milk at the dining room's buffet hatch
quest.ship_cat.bosun.log: I have the milk. Now to the bow, to the hatch. The bosun rules there from eight till noon. Past him with milk in my pocket... All right. I'll try.
quest.ship_cat.bring_milk.obj: Carry the milk to the bow past Taras the bosun
quest.ship_cat.tell.log: The bosun knows everything. The cat is called Bosun, she has sailed as a stowaway for three years, and she has three kittens in the hold. He told me to tell no one, Zoya least of all. And Zoya is waiting for me to tell.
quest.ship_telegram.title: A Telegram for Swallow
quest.ship_telegram.desc: The radio operator has a telegram with no surname and no cabin on it. Someone at the other end is waiting for an answer.
quest.ship_telegram.done: The telegram has gone. Lev Markovich says "papa" in Morse sounds like footsteps on a staircase. Now I hear it too.
quest.ship_telegram.take.log: The radio room is on the boat deck, behind the funnel. Lev Markovich, the operator, sits there from eight to eight in his headphones, talking to the shore in dots and dashes.
quest.ship_telegram.talk_lev.obj: Talk to Lev Markovich, the radio operator
quest.ship_telegram.ask.log: The telegram: "Motor ship Polden. To Swallow. No longer angry. Expecting you both. Papa." No surname, no cabin. Lev Markovich says to ask Nonna Arkadyevna, the purser: she has the passenger list and a memory like a radar. Her desk is on the main deck, by the gangway.
quest.ship_telegram.ask_nonna.obj: Ask Nonna Arkadyevna who Swallow is
quest.ship_telegram.find.log: Nonna Arkadyevna worked it out: "you both" means Swallow isn't travelling alone. The honeymooners, cabin twelve on the promenade deck. Olya signed the list with her maiden name, crossed it out and wrote the new one. I'm to go myself: "you're just a boy with a telegram".
quest.ship_telegram.find_olya.obj: Find Swallow and read her the telegram
quest.ship_telegram.reply.log: Swallow is Olya. They married without her father. I've learnt the answer by heart: "Papa. Back on Sunday. Bake the pie. Both your swallows." Take it to Lev Markovich.
quest.ship_telegram.reply_lev.obj: Give the radio operator the answer
quest.ship_sharp.title: The Card Sharp from Riga
quest.ship_sharp.desc: The "engineer from Riga" has been lucky at the card table three voyages running. Givi the barman doesn't believe in luck like that.
quest.ship_sharp.done: I saw it. The bottom card left the pack so smoothly it was almost beautiful. Now to decide: tell Givi, and then it all goes by the rules, or speak to Albert myself.
quest.ship_sharp.hint.log: The bar is on the promenade deck, next to the music saloon. Givi stands behind it from ten in the morning till one at night, telling stories. He pours me nothing but lemonade.
quest.ship_sharp.watch_hands.log: Givi asks me to sit in at the card table. It gathers in the saloon after ten at night, and you can play for matches. When Albert deals, watch his hands, not the cards. If I see something, no shouting.
quest.ship_sharp.catch_albert.obj: Sit in at the card table and catch Albert's hands when he deals
quest.ship_sharp_word.title: The Card Sharp: A Quiet Word
quest.ship_sharp_word.desc: I could tell no one and go to Albert myself.
quest.ship_sharp_word.done: Albert used to mend watches. The workshop closed and the hands stayed. He said he would give the money back, and for some reason I believe him.
quest.ship_sharp_word.talk.log: By day Albert smokes aft, on the smoking deck; from ten at night he is at cards. Walk up and say what I saw. A bit scary.
quest.ship_sharp_report.title: The Card Sharp: By the Rules
quest.ship_sharp_report.desc: I could tell Givi everything, and he'll report to the purser. That's the proper way.
quest.ship_sharp_report.done: Givi said there would be no scene: a talk with Nonna Arkadyevna and a list of what goes back to whom. By the rules it turns out quiet. I thought it would be louder.
quest.ship_sharp_report.tell.log: Givi is behind the bar from ten in the morning till one at night. Tell him about the bottom card.
quest.ship_pilot.title: Vera Ignatyevna's Pilot Book
quest.ship_pilot.desc: A geography teacher pointed at these islands with a stick for thirty years and never saw one. She has a list and a schoolboy's pencil.
quest.ship_pilot.done: Three islands ticked with Kolya Lapshin's pencil. Vera Ignatyevna pointed at them for thirty years; I looked at them for half an hour. I think geography and I are even.
quest.ship_pilot.islands.log: An island. A real one, not on a map. An old teacher stood beside me at the rail with a list, whispering the names: the Stone Brothers, the Needle's Eye, Bird Island, the Far Light, Long Island, the Seal Rocks. She ticks each one she sees, but she can't stand at the rail for long: the wind. I'll look for her. The bow or a bridge wing is best, and what comes when is in the "Pilot of the Islands" in the ship's library.
quest.ship_pilot.see_three.obj: See three islands from the deck
quest.ship_pilot.read_pilot.obj: Read the "Pilot of the Islands" in the ship's library
quest.ship_pilot.tell.log: Three islands done. I've kept one thing about each, but a real one. Vera Ignatyevna reads in the library on the promenade deck in the mornings and comes out to the rail when an island is in sight.
quest.ship_pilot.tell_vera.obj: Tell Vera Ignatyevna what I saw
quest.ship_waltz.title: The First Waltz
quest.ship_waltz.desc: The honeymooners in cabin twelve have fallen out, and Saturday is the captain's dinner with dancing. The husband has been "getting some air" aft for two hours.
quest.ship_waltz.done: Misha counted with his lips all through the waltz and trod on Olya's foot four times. She says it was the best waltz of her life. Grown-ups have an odd way of counting "best".
quest.ship_waltz.misha.log: Aft, where people smoke, a tall man in a grey jacket has stood for two hours, not smoking. Red ears. That's Misha, the bridegroom from cabin twelve. His wife sits on a promenade deck bench looking not at the sea but at the door. They both come to table on the minute and sit side by side: mealtimes are the surest place to catch him.
quest.ship_waltz.talk_misha.obj: Talk to Misha, the bridegroom from cabin twelve
quest.ship_waltz.tune.log: Misha can't dance. At all. At the wedding he got away with it, but Saturday is the captain's dinner and a waltz in front of the captain, and Olya has brought her dress in a suitcase of its own. He asks me to find out from the grey-haired pianist what they'll play first: perhaps not a waltz. Blum and his quartet are in the music saloon: at the concert in the evening, at rehearsal from eleven on Saturday.
quest.ship_waltz.talk_blum.obj: Ask Blum the pianist what they play first
quest.ship_waltz.lesson.log: The first will be a waltz, "Waves of the Amur": otherwise the captain doesn't know the evening has begun. But Blum promised to play slowly and sent a message: a waltz goes up to three. One, step; two, close; three, stand and find you're alive. I'm carrying this to Misha.
quest.ship_waltz.teach_misha.obj: Tell Misha how a waltz is counted
quest.ship_waltz.ball.log: Misha was counting to four, that was the whole trouble. Now he counts to three and walks round a lifeboat. The dancing is on Saturday from half past eight in the music saloon. He asked me to come: "if I fall, at least someone can say it looked good". I'll have to step onto the floor myself.
quest.ship_waltz.dance.obj: Come to the dancing in the music saloon and step onto the floor
quest.ship_waltz.after.log: They danced. He counted with his lips, you could see it across the whole saloon. Find Misha and tell him it looked good: I promised.
quest.ship_waltz.hear_misha.obj: Talk to Misha after the waltz
quest.ship_watch.title: The Watch
quest.ship_watch.desc: Helmsman Vitya Chizh is in his first season. From seven in the evening till midnight he is alone in the wheelhouse, and after ten it seems to him that he is the only one awake in the whole ship.
quest.ship_watch.done: I went forward at night and struck the bell once, so the helmsman would know he was not the only one awake. I never thought you could help someone just by not being asleep.
quest.ship_watch.fear.log: At the wheel stands a lad not much older than me. Vitya Chizh, helmsman. He steers from eight till noon and from half past six in the evening till midnight, and eats in the dining saloon before everyone else.
quest.ship_watch.bell.log: In the evening Vitya is alone in the wheelhouse: the captain is at dinner, the chief mate asleep before her own watch. After ten the deck lights are turned down and there is nothing ahead but black water. He asks me to go forward at night and strike the bell once, softly: he can't turn round, but he can hear. The bell hangs on the foredeck. By day it is not to be touched: by day the bell tells the time.
quest.ship_watch.strike_bell.obj: After ten at night, strike the ship's bell in the bows
quest.ship_watch.tell.log: I struck it, once. The sound went through the whole ship and took a long time to end. Now to ask Vitya whether he heard: he is at the wheel till midnight and from eight in the morning, and breakfasts in the dining saloon just after seven.
quest.ship_watch.tell_vitya.obj: Ask Vitya whether he heard the bell
quest.ship_diesel.title: The Chief and His Diesel
quest.ship_diesel.desc: Chief Engineer Einar Kask, "Grandad" as ships call the chief, has heard a knock in the engine for three days that nobody else hears.
quest.ship_diesel.done: The knock was real: a nut on the third cylinder, a quarter turn. Grandad Einar hears the diesel the way Lev Markovich hears the air. And he won't go ashore because in the quiet you hear what knocks in yourself, and no spanner reaches there.
quest.ship_diesel.knock.log: On the main deck there is a door to the engine room and a gallery over the diesel. The chief engineer, "Grandad", stands there from eight to eight, listening. They say he's Estonian and can keep silent a whole watch.
quest.ship_diesel.talk_einar.obj: Talk to Einar, the chief engineer
quest.ship_diesel.rag.log: Grandad hears a knock: once every four seconds, for three days. The engineers say he imagines it. He can't leave the engine. He needs a clean white rag, the cook has those, and a twenty-seven spanner: the drummer borrowed it. First the galley, Aunt Pasha, she's there from six in the morning till eight at night.
quest.ship_diesel.ask_pasha.obj: Ask Aunt Pasha for a clean rag
quest.ship_diesel.key.log: Aunt Pasha gave me no rag. She gave a handkerchief, linen, ironed: "a rag he'd throw away, a handkerchief he'll return". Now the twenty-seven spanner. Kostya Yozh, the quartet's drummer, borrowed it. The quartet is in the music saloon: at the concert in the evening, at rehearsal from eleven on Saturday.
quest.ship_diesel.ask_kostya.obj: Ask Kostya the drummer for the twenty-seven spanner
quest.ship_diesel.give.log: The spanner, it turns out, is with Grandad himself: Kostya returned it back on Thursday and put it in Grandad's drawer, under the log, so it wouldn't get lost. And Grandad never looks under the log: he knows it by heart. Take him the handkerchief and tell him about the drawer.
quest.ship_birds.title: The Bird Colony
quest.ship_birds.desc: Mr Mori has counted the birds of Bird Island for six years. He has two hands, and there are four species on the cliff.
quest.ship_birds.done: Ninety guillemots, one gull called Captain and a notebook with a drawing where my hand is worse than the bird. Mori-san apologised that I'll never be able to just look at the sky again. I don't mind.
quest.ship_birds.meet.log: On the boat deck, at the rail, stands a man with a telescope on a tripod and a notebook. Haruto Mori, from Sapporo. He's almost always there, even when there are no birds.
quest.ship_birds.count.log: Mori-san counts birds for a society in Sapporo: one hour a year, while the ship goes round Bird Island. He counts the kittiwakes and has trusted me with the guillemots on the north ledge: they stand like penguins, all alike. Count in tens. "An error is allowed, a lie is not." Saturday, ten till half past eleven, boat deck, the bench by the funnel.
quest.ship_birds.count_birds.obj: Count the guillemots from the boat deck while the ship rounds Bird Island
quest.ship_birds.report.log: Counted. In tens, as told. It came to about ninety: four rows on the ledge, all facing the rock. In the last ten one guillemot dived. Report to Mori-san.
quest.ship_birds.report_haruto.obj: Report the guillemot count to Mr Mori
quest.ship_birds.gull.log: Ninety is entered, "observer: a local youth". Now a personal request: a herring gull with a dark spot on its bill has followed the stern for six years; Mori-san calls it Captain. Feed it from the stern: when it takes bread it hangs in the air, and he has time to draw. The kiosk and the buffet sell bubliki.
quest.ship_birds.feed_gull.obj: Feed the gulls from the stern rail
quest.ship_birds.sketch.log: The gull with the spot on its bill took the bublik right from my fingers and hung in the air for a second. Mori-san got something down in that time.
quest.ship_birds.see_sketch.obj: See what Mr Mori has drawn
quest.ship_games.title: The Deck Biathlon
quest.ship_games.desc: Rimma the entertainer has a plan for joy: forty-two people a voyage. I've been put down as the forty-first.
quest.ship_games.done: I was given my certificate "before the sea", there being nobody else about. Every voyage Rimma writes herself down as the forty-second if she's a person short. Today she wasn't.
quest.ship_games.enroll.log: Rimma Volskaya, the entertainer, carries a whistle and a notepad and turns up wherever two people stand idle. Usually she's in the music saloon, at morning exercise on the boat deck, and at the deck games from half past eleven on Saturday.
quest.ship_games.play.log: I've been entered in the deck biathlon as "ship's boy". I have to win at ring toss, aft on the promenade deck, and at shuffleboard on the boat deck. Rimma promises the winner a certificate with the captain's seal. A real seal, she says: she stamps it herself.
quest.ship_games.win_rings.obj: Win at ring toss on the after deck
quest.ship_games.win_shuffle.obj: Win at shuffleboard on the boat deck
quest.ship_games.award.log: Won both. The rings were harder: the deck rolls and the peg doesn't. Report to Rimma.
quest.ship_key.title: Grandmother's Suitcase
quest.ship_key.desc: Senya, aged ten, has lost the key of his grandmother's suitcase. Inside is the present for his mother. Grandmother thinks the key is in his sock.
quest.ship_key.done: The key lay where Senya had buried it as treasure, so as not to lose it. And Granny Faina, it turns out, has worn a spare round her neck since forty-six. She kept quiet so he would find it himself. On this ship everyone keeps quiet very kindly.
quest.ship_key.secret.log: On the boat deck, by the deck chairs, a boy of about ten is looking under each one in turn and pretending to tie his shoelace. Beside him his grandmother knits in a deck chair.
quest.ship_key.search.log: The key is on a green tape. In the suitcase is a shawl, Granny Faina knitted it for his mother for two years, and his mother meets them on Sunday. Senya was playing pirates: he looked under the lifeboat's cover, the deck chairs were an island, and under a bench on the promenade deck he had his treasure. Look in all three places. Not a word to Granny.
quest.ship_key.look_bench.obj: Look under a bench on the promenade deck
quest.ship_key.open.log: Nothing in two places, and in the third, right in the crack, a key on a green tape with a wooden sword beside it. A proper treasure. Take it to Senya before Granny asks about the sock again.
quest.ship_captain.title: The Captain's Hour
quest.ship_captain.desc: On the Polden everything that happens is reported to the captain sooner or later. I seem to have been reported too.
quest.ship_captain.done: Captain Gromov waited forty days in the ice for four minutes of sun. That is why the ship is called Polden, "noon": so that he has a noon every day. I held the wheel for one minute. I have his binoculars now. They show you well the thing you're waiting for.
quest.ship_captain.bridge.log: Zoya brought a note on the purser's form: "You are invited to the bridge. Not 'may drop in': invited. N. A. Lisitskaya. P.S. Comb your hair." The bridge is at the very top, beyond the boat deck. Captain Gromov has the watch from eight till noon and from four till seven.
quest.ship_captain.talk_gromov.obj: Go up to Captain Gromov on the bridge
quest.ship_captain.wheel.log: The captain stood me to the right of the helmsman and told me to take the wheel. "Hold her for a minute. A minute at the wheel is longer than one ashore." The wheel is in the middle of the wheelhouse, wooden, warm from hands.
quest.ship_captain.hold_wheel.obj: Take the wheel and hold the course
quest.ship_captain.story.log: The minute is up. It really is longer. The captain is looking at me and seems about to tell me something.
line.hero.ship_blum_waltz_tune.1: Maestro, what do you play first on Saturday?
line.hero.ship_blum_waltz_tune.3: Could it not be a waltz? There's a man who can't.
line.hero.ship_einar_diesel_give.2: And you have the spanner. In the drawer, under the log.
line.hero.ship_givi_sharp_report.1: Givi, he deals from the bottom. I saw it.
line.hero.ship_haruto_birds_report.1: About ninety guillemots. Four rows on the ledge. One dived, I counted it.
line.hero.ship_lev_tg_reply.1: Found her. The answer is: "Papa. Back on Sunday. Bake the pie. Both your swallows."
line.hero.ship_misha_waltz_lesson.1: A waltz first. But he'll play it slowly. And a waltz goes up to three. One, step; two, close; three, stand.
line.hero.ship_olya_tg_found.1: A telegram for you. I think. "To Swallow. No longer angry. Expecting you both. Papa."
line.hero.ship_vais_watch_mate.2: Will you tell him he's managing?
line.hero.ship_vera_pilot_tell.1: I saw three. One thing about each. The main one: they're much smaller than I thought. And much farther away.
line.hero.ship_zoya_cat_tell.2: A cat. With kittens. But it's a secret. From you. The bosun asked.
line.ship_albert.back.1: You again. And me again. Neither of us, it seems, knows how to get off in time.
line.ship_albert.first.1: Good afternoon. Albert. An engineer, from Riga. You don't play cards? Quite right. I do, and what good has it done me.
line.ship_albert.hands.1: Watch how a gull takes bread on the wing. Not one unnecessary movement. All my life I've respected exact hands. Even when they're wings.
line.ship_albert.luck.1: They say I'm lucky. Luck, young man, is when nobody asks why.
line.ship_albert.riga.1: It's raining in Riga now. It always rains there when I leave. The city pretends it doesn't care.
line.ship_albert.sat.1: Ah, it's you. You looked at me for a long time yesterday. Never mind, I'm used to it. People look at me with admiration or with suspicion. Yours is, so far, a third kind.
line.ship_albert.sharp_done.1: Today I played honestly and lost three roubles. A strange feeling. Like taking off tight shoes.
line.ship_albert.sharp_word.2: Sit down. Don't stand over me like a conscience. What exactly did you see?
line.ship_albert.sharp_word.4: A good eye. In Riga I mended watches. The workshop closed and the hands stayed. Hands need something to do.
line.ship_albert.sharp_word.5: I'll return the money. To Taras through the barman: he's proud, he won't take it otherwise. And a word for you: whoever watches other people's hands instead of his own cards can't lose any more. I had that look once. Long ago.
line.ship_albert.sharp_word_late.1: Ah, it's you. Nonna Arkadyevna has been already. Very polite, very quiet. I shall return it all. I go ashore on Sunday and won't buy another ticket.
line.ship_albert.sharp_word_late.2: Don't apologise. You did it by the rules. All my life I've envied people who can do things by the rules.
line.ship_albert.sun.1: Ashore today. I dislike Sundays: everything you've won becomes mere money.
line.ship_albert.sun_cloudy.1: A grey sky. As in Riga. I'm at ease in this weather: nothing glitters, nothing distracts.
line.ship_albert.sun_low.1: I don't play at sunset. Superstition. The light's too good: you can see faces.
line.ship_albert.sun_night.1: At night everyone at the table is more honest than by day. They lose honestly, they get angry honestly. Only I am polite, as ever.
line.ship_albert.watches.1: Your watch is two minutes fast. I can hear it. Don't ask how. Just put it right.
line.ship_asta.back.1: You came back. Then I didn't come back for nothing either.
line.ship_asta.blum.1: Saveliy says I play as if I were leaving. He's right. But every time I come back for the last bar.
line.ship_asta.breath.1: A clarinet is breath that's been given a road. So on deck I just breathe. I'm rehearsing.
line.ship_asta.first.1: Hello. I'm Asta. Clarinet, sometimes saxophone. You don't smoke? Good. Stand by me then, the wind's right here.
line.ship_asta.gulls.1: The gulls cry in E flat. I've checked. When I play in E flat they go quiet and listen. Or take offence.
line.ship_asta.north.1: I'm from the north. Our sea is grey and serious. This one is warm and jokes all the time. I've been getting used to it for three years.
line.ship_asta.sat.1: You're here again. Good. Yesterday I played one phrase for you, in the middle of the second number. You didn't notice. That's as it should be.
line.ship_asta.sun.1: On Sundays I always think this is my last voyage. And on Friday I'm standing at the gangway with my case. The clarinet decides for me.
line.ship_asta.sun_cloudy.1: Today it's like home. Grey sky, grey water and no seam between them. I play better in this weather.
line.ship_asta.sun_low.1: Look at that path from the sun. Straight to us. Every evening I wonder whether you could walk away along it. And every evening I have a concert.
line.ship_asta.sun_night.1: At night on the stern you can hear the screw stirring the water. As if someone very large were stirring tea.
line.ship_blum.back.1: Ah, my listener! The third row is free. I told Rimma to seat nobody there.
line.ship_blum.first.1: Good day, child. Do you play anything? No? Never mind. Listening is an instrument too, and a rare one.
line.ship_blum.piano.1: A piano at sea goes out of tune with the damp. Every Friday I talk it round. By Saturday it agrees; on Sunday we are both tired.
line.ship_blum.quartet.1: The Noonday Quartet. Named after the ship, and we mostly play in the evenings. It has amused me for eleven years.
line.ship_blum.requests.1: Shall I play something for you? Not now, this evening. Come up and say: "Maestro, for the ship's boy." I'll understand.
line.ship_blum.sat.1: Yesterday you sat in the third row and didn't clap. You listened. Musicians see that from the stage, child. It's worth more to us.
line.ship_blum.sun.1: No concert today. On Sundays I play while everyone goes down the gangway. Nobody listens, they're all carrying suitcases. But they walk in time.
line.ship_blum.sun_low.1: At sunset I always play the same piece, quietly, for myself. I won't say which. Whoever hears it, hears it.
line.ship_blum.sun_night.1: After a concert the piano stays warm for an hour. I sit beside it. We don't talk, we cool down.
line.ship_blum.waltz_done.1: The bridegroom didn't fall. The bride cried. The bass went flat from feeling. A good waltz, child.
line.ship_blum.waltz_slow.1: Did you tell him? Good. I've already told the bass: on Saturday we play the first number as if carrying a sleeping child.
line.ship_blum.waltz_tune.2: A waltz, child. At the captain's dinner the first is always a waltz: otherwise the captain doesn't know the evening has begun.
line.ship_blum.waltz_tune.4: The bridegroom? Grey jacket? He's walked past my piano for three hours, counting in a whisper. Only to four. Tell him a waltz goes up to three. One, step; two, close; three, stand and find you're alive.
line.ship_blum.waltz_tune.5: And tell him I'll play it slowly. "Waves of the Amur" can go so slowly even a technologist will learn. Thirty years I've played at weddings: it isn't those who can't dance that fall, it's those who never step out.
line.ship_blum.weddings.1: I played at weddings for thirty years. Know which music is hardest? The kind people are silent to. It's seldom asked for and remembered for life.
line.ship_einar.back.1: Tere. You. She remembers you. So do I.
line.ship_einar.diesel_done.1: Eight hundred revolutions. Even. I've washed the handkerchief. Pasha gets it back on Sunday. Ironed.
line.ship_einar.diesel_give.3: ...Yes. Under the log. Watch. I run it along the pipe. White: clean. White: clean. And here, a drop. Injector nut, third cylinder. A quarter turn.
line.ship_einar.diesel_give.5: Every autumn they call me ashore, to the workshops. Warm, eight hours, Saturdays off. I tried. Ashore it's quiet. In the quiet you hear what knocks in yourself. And no spanner reaches there.
line.ship_einar.diesel_give.6: Take this. Amber, from our shore. There's a little fly in it. She too stayed where she was happy.
line.ship_einar.diesel_knock.3: The diesel is eight hundred revolutions. And under them: knock. Once in four seconds. Three days now.
line.ship_einar.diesel_knock.4: They say: Grandad, you imagine it. I don't. I need a rag, clean, white, from the cook. And the twenty-seven spanner: the drummer took it, Yozh. I can't leave: I go, and it knocks without me.
line.ship_einar.diesel_wait.1: A rag. White. From the cook. The spanner from the drummer.
line.ship_einar.first.1: Tere. Touch nothing with your hands. You may look. You should listen.
line.ship_einar.name.1: They call me "Grandad". In the fleet that's what they call the chief. I was thirty when I became Grandad. I'm used to it.
line.ship_einar.oil.1: The oil is warm. Feel the pipe. Here you may. Warm means alive.
line.ship_einar.revs.1: Eight hundred revolutions. Six cylinders. Twenty-two years. Not one major overhaul.
line.ship_einar.sat.1: You've come again. Good. Yesterday you looked. Today you listen. That is the right order.
line.ship_einar.sun.1: At six I shall stop her. She doesn't like it. Nor do I. Till Friday.
line.ship_einar.sun_day.1: The sun. I see it at dinner time. Ten minutes. It's enough.
line.ship_einar.sun_night.1: At night she sounds lower. The water's colder. I sleep when I hear her go lower.
line.ship_einar.talk.1: They say I talk little. The diesel talks little too. We understand each other.
line.ship_faina.back.1: You again too! Senka and I are regulars now. I'm not afraid of the sea any more. All I'm afraid of now is the tickets running out.
line.ship_faina.first.1: Sit down, sonny, don't stand over me. Whose boy are you? Travelling alone? Brave. At your age the only place I went alone was to the well.
line.ship_faina.food.1: The food's good. The cook knows her business. I'd salt the borscht differently, but I shan't tell her. Two housewives in one galley make a gale.
line.ship_faina.key_done.1: My daughter will like the shawl. And Senka knows now that treasure gets written down. Thank you for not giving him away. I didn't either.
line.ship_faina.key_knows.1: Looking for a key? Look, look. I've had the spare round my neck since forty-six. But a man ought to find what he's lost himself, at least once in his life.
line.ship_faina.knit.1: Knitting. What, I won't say: I don't know myself. The hands knit, and we'll see. It usually turns out a sock.
line.ship_faina.sat.1: Ah, sonny. Senka's been buzzing in my ears about you. "A big boy, travelling on his own." Don't you send him away. He likes being with the big ones.
line.ship_faina.sea.1: I was afraid of the sea. Lived by it all my life and was afraid. And Senka says: Granny, let's go. So I went. Turns out it was a bit afraid of me too.
line.ship_faina.senya.1: My Senka takes after his grandfather. He lost everything too. Only me he didn't lose, held on for fifty years.
line.ship_faina.sun.1: Well, that's that, sonny. Two days, and it's like a month's stay with relations. Only relations don't feed you this well.
line.ship_faina.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast, and the needles are cold. You knit tighter in this weather. Senka won't get this sock onto one foot.
line.ship_faina.sun_day.1: It's good in the sun. Warms the bones. I've become like a cat: wherever the sun is, that's where I shift my deck chair.
line.ship_faina.sun_low.1: Sunset. My old man used to say: the sun goes down so that we'll miss it. So I miss it till morning. Him too.
line.ship_givi.back.1: Vai! Look who it is! Lemonade? I remember. Givi remembers everyone, that's Givi's job.
line.ship_givi.bar.1: Fourteen years behind a bar. Know what I've learned? People don't come to drink. People come so that someone is standing opposite.
line.ship_givi.cocktail.1: My milk cocktail is the best on this sea. The secret's simple: shake till your arm's tired, and then one minute more.
line.ship_givi.first.1: Gamarjoba, genatsvale! Sit down. What'll it be? Lemonade, kvass, coffee, a milk cocktail. Don't ask for wine: none for you, and I mustn't.
line.ship_givi.first.3: The right choice. My grandfather said: he who starts with lemonade remembers longer what the talk was about.
line.ship_givi.grandfather.1: My grandfather lived a hundred and four years in the mountains and never saw the sea. He'd say: what do I want the sea for, I've the sky. I brought him some in a bottle. He tasted it: "Oversalted."
line.ship_givi.sat.1: Yesterday you sat at the end. Today you sat in the middle. Tomorrow you'll be helping me dry glasses, I know how it goes.
line.ship_givi.sharp_hint.1: Genatsvale, sit. The lemonade's on the house, the talk's on you.
line.ship_givi.sharp_hint.2: See the engineer from Riga? Albert. Winning three voyages now. He won Taras's pay and Lev Markovich's watch. Gave the watch back, handsomely.
line.ship_givi.sharp_hint.3: My grandfather said: lucky three times, a lucky man. Lucky four times, he's the one dealing. I can't see from behind the bar. You sit in, after ten.
line.ship_givi.sharp_hint.4: When he deals, don't look at your cards. Watch his hands. If you see it, don't shout. Come to me. Or not to me. You'll decide.
line.ship_givi.sharp_report.2: You saw. So old Givi wasn't imagining it. Thank you for coming here and not shouting it across the saloon.
line.ship_givi.sharp_report.3: I'll tell Nonna Arkadyevna. No scene: half an hour's talk and a list of what goes back to whom. And one name fewer next voyage.
line.ship_givi.sharp_report.4: You know what's a pity, genatsvale? He's the best talker at this bar. Catching a man's hand is easy. Not being sorry afterwards is the hard part.
line.ship_givi.sharp_report_done.1: The table's honest now. Honesty, genatsvale, is like mineral water: good for you, but you can't make a toast with it.
line.ship_givi.sharp_report_late.1: You spoke to him yourself? And he promised to pay it back? Then old Givi heard nothing. But I'll whisper to Nonna Arkadyevna to sit by the table with her knitting. Knitting disciplines card players wonderfully.
line.ship_givi.sharp_wait.1: The table gathers after ten. Play for matches, for the fun of it. And when Albert deals: his hands, watch his hands.
line.ship_givi.sharp_word_done.1: An envelope came for Taras today, through me. He asked who from. I said: from the sea. He believed it, genatsvale. He's a bosun, after all.
line.ship_givi.sun.1: The last lemonade, genatsvale. This one's on the house. Farewells are always on the house, or people don't come back.
line.ship_givi.sun_cloudy.1: Gloomy today. In weather like this I sell twice the coffee. I'll make yours weak, so you'll sleep afterwards.
line.ship_givi.sun_low.1: See the sunset in the porthole? The colour of good tea. I compare them every evening. Tea still wins every other time.
line.ship_givi.sun_night.1: At night a bar is like a lighthouse: a light on, a man standing. They don't come in for lemonade. They come to make sure it's lit.
line.ship_givi.toast.1: Want a toast with your lemonade? To those at sea. And to those ashore who think we're out here on holiday.
line.ship_gromov.back.1: With us again? Then the sea has entered you in its list. It keeps a list of its own, and you can't apply.
line.ship_gromov.cap_bridge.1: Come in. Stand here, to the right of the helmsman. On the left stands the one who answers for it.
line.ship_gromov.cap_bridge.2: It has been reported to me that there is someone on my ship doing more than his ticket says. Such people I am obliged to know by sight.
line.ship_gromov.cap_bridge.3: Take the wheel. Don't be afraid, the helmsman is beside you. Hold her for a minute. A minute at the wheel is longer than one ashore.
line.ship_gromov.cap_done.1: At noon come up on deck. Just stand a while. You needn't take your cap off, we're not in the ice. But I take mine off.
line.ship_gromov.cap_story.1: One minute. Course steady. Officer of the watch, enter it: a passenger stood at the wheel, no remarks.
line.ship_gromov.cap_story.2: You haven't asked why "Polden", noon. Everyone asks. I sailed twenty years in the ice. In winter there is no noon there: the sun doesn't rise, and the clock shows twelve out of mere politeness.
line.ship_gromov.cap_story.3: Once we were beset for forty days. On the forty-first, at noon, the rim of the sun showed over the ice ridges. For four minutes. The whole crew stood on deck bareheaded. Nobody gave the order.
line.ship_gromov.cap_story.4: When they gave me this ship and asked what to call her, I said: Polden. So that I should have a noon every day. I have not slept through one since.
line.ship_gromov.cap_story.5: Take these binoculars. They were there with me. They show you well the thing you are waiting for.
line.ship_gromov.cap_wheel.1: The wheel is in front of you. Don't look at it, look ahead. A ship goes where her helmsman looks.
line.ship_gromov.chair.1: One place at the captain's table is always free. It isn't for the authorities. It's for whoever comes with a good story.
line.ship_gromov.crew.1: I have a good crew. Each of them hears something: the operator the air, the chief his diesel, the purser everything else.
line.ship_gromov.first.1: A passenger? Welcome aboard the Polden. We have three rules: don't fall overboard, don't be late for dinner, do look at the sunset.
line.ship_gromov.first.3: The third is the main one. Nonna Arkadyevna thought up the first two.
line.ship_gromov.ice.1: In the ice I spent twenty years counting degrees below zero. Here I count gulls. The gulls are harder to make add up.
line.ship_gromov.sat.1: The second day. From today a passenger stops asking where the dining room is and starts asking where we are. That's a sailor already.
line.ship_gromov.speed.1: We're making nine knots. No need for more: the islands aren't going anywhere, and dinner would get cold.
line.ship_gromov.sun.1: We'll be on the roads by six. Going ashore is always a little sad. I've been going ashore for forty years and still haven't got used to it.
line.ship_gromov.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast. The sun's in its place, only without witnesses. In the ice I learned to take its word for it.
line.ship_gromov.sun_day.1: At noon I step out onto the bridge wing. A habit. With a name like this ship's you can't not.
line.ship_gromov.sun_low.1: Look at the sunset. It's included in the price of the ticket, but not everyone collects.
line.ship_gromov.sun_night.1: At night the sea is more honest. You see only lights, and every light means something.
line.ship_haruto.back.1: You are here again. Birds also return to the same ledge. It is called site fidelity. A very good quality.
line.ship_haruto.birds_done.1: I have sent the figures to Sapporo. The column "observers" now says two. For six years it said one.
line.ship_haruto.birds_gull.1: The stern, the rail. You need a bublik: the kiosk and the buffet sell them. The gull with the spot on its bill. The others are merely gulls.
line.ship_haruto.birds_meet.1: Excuse me. Have you two hands free? Mine are both taken, and there are four species of bird.
line.ship_haruto.birds_meet.2: I am Mori. I count birds for a society in Sapporo. Six years this island, one hour each year, while the ship goes round.
line.ship_haruto.birds_meet.3: On the north ledge are guillemots. They stand like penguins, all alike. I count kittiwakes, that is harder. You count the guillemots. In tens. An error is allowed, a lie is not.
line.ship_haruto.birds_meet.5: Saturday, ten o'clock, Bird Island. Boat deck, the bench by the funnel. Do not be late: the island does not wait, nor does the ship.
line.ship_haruto.birds_report.2: Ninety. I write: observer, a local youth. Last year it was eighty-two. You have brought good news.
line.ship_haruto.birds_report.3: Now a personal request. A herring gull with a dark spot on its bill follows the stern. Six years. I call it Captain. Feed it from the stern: when it takes bread it hangs, and I have time to draw.
line.ship_haruto.birds_sketch.1: I had time. Look: here she is, here is your hand. The hand I drew badly, the bird well. That is as it should be with an ornithologist.
line.ship_haruto.birds_sketch.2: The notebook is yours. It has many clean pages left. We say: one who has once counted birds can no longer simply look at the sky. Forgive me for that.
line.ship_haruto.birds_wait.1: Saturday, ten till half past eleven. The bench by the funnel. Count in tens.
line.ship_haruto.first.1: Good afternoon. Forgive me for not turning round: there is a cormorant to port. My name is Mori. I watch birds.
line.ship_haruto.patience.1: You cannot call a bird. You can only be where it will be. That is all I know how to do.
line.ship_haruto.russian.1: I learned Russian from a field guide to birds. So I know the word for "grebe" but not how to ask for the salt.
line.ship_haruto.sat.1: Good morning. Today at ten, Bird Island. I have not slept. I never sleep before the island, six years now.
line.ship_haruto.scope.1: Would you like to look through the telescope? Do not touch the tripod. Look with one eye, do not close the other. Yes. Now you see a kilometre.
line.ship_haruto.six.1: This is my sixth year. From Sapporo it is three days' journey. My wife says: there are birds at home too. She is right. But these are different ones.
line.ship_haruto.sun.1: Today I add it up. Thirty-one species this voyage. Last year twenty-nine. The world is richer by two species. Or I am more attentive.
line.ship_haruto.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast. Better for observation: no glare. Worse for the heart. I write down both.
line.ship_haruto.sun_day.1: At noon the birds are silent. It is hot, there is no shade. I am silent too. We respect noon.
line.ship_haruto.sun_low.1: At sunset the gulls fly against the sun and you see every feather through and through. I do not write it down. It is not for writing down.
line.ship_inga.back.1: You. I developed that frame of you at the rail. You can see in it that you'd come back. I'm not surprised.
line.ship_inga.captain.1: I've been photographing the captain for three voyages. He's never once looked at the lens. He looks where the ship is going. I have to run ahead.
line.ship_inga.faces.1: The best faces on a ship are on the second day after lunch. People have forgotten how they're supposed to look and haven't yet remembered they're soon going home.
line.ship_inga.film.1: I have thirty-six frames for the whole voyage. One film. On purpose. When frames are few you look more honestly.
line.ship_inga.first.1: Stay like that. Don't move. The light's good. ...Done, thanks. I'm Inga. I photograph people who don't know they're being photographed. You know now, so it doesn't count.
line.ship_inga.hands.1: I like photographing hands more than faces. Faces can pretend. Hands can't: look how the bosun holds a rope and how a passenger holds the rail.
line.ship_inga.sat.1: I took you yesterday. At the rail, from behind. You were looking at the town and it was getting smaller. A good frame. The twenty-ninth.
line.ship_inga.sun.1: One frame left. I'm saving it for the gangway: somebody always turns to look back. That's the one I'll take.
line.ship_inga.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast isn't bad light. It's soft light. Wrinkles neither lie nor shout in it. Old people should only be photographed like this.
line.ship_inga.sun_day.1: I don't shoot at noon. The light's from above, shadows under the eyes, everyone looks tired. Noon you simply wait out, like a rest in music.
line.ship_inga.sun_low.1: There. Now. For ten minutes a day the light makes everyone beautiful and a little sad. They're what I come for.
line.ship_inga.tg_notme.1: Swallow? My father called me "Exposure": I couldn't sit still a minute as a child. Not for me. But I'd photograph the face of whoever it is for.
line.ship_kostya.back.1: Hello, offbeat! With us again? Sit near the drums, I'll wink at you on the break.
line.ship_kostya.brushes.1: Blum makes me play with brushes. With sticks, he says, I'd frighten the honeymooners. But with brushes I can make it sound like rain on the deck.
line.ship_kostya.diesel_key.1: The twenty-seven spanner? I gave it back! Thursday. Put it in Grandad's drawer, under the log, so it wouldn't get lost.
line.ship_kostya.diesel_key.2: He hasn't found it? He never looks under the log, he knows it by heart.
line.ship_kostya.diesel_key.3: And tell him the cymbal hasn't rattled since. He was the only one on the whole ship who heard it rattle. Even I didn't, and I play the thing.
line.ship_kostya.diesel_key_again.1: In the drawer, under the log. On the left. No, the right. Under the log for sure.
line.ship_kostya.dream.1: Some day I want to play a solo on the ship's bell. The bosun said: over his dead body. I said: that's a rhythm too.
line.ship_kostya.first.1: Hi! You're new? I'm Kostya, drums. Surname Yozh, "hedgehog", honest. With both dots in my passport.
line.ship_kostya.rhythm.1: Hear the diesel? Four-four, dead even. I can tap my fingers to it all night. Otar, my cabin mate, doesn't object. He doesn't object to anything.
line.ship_kostya.rolling.1: When she rolls the cymbals play themselves. Blum says it's the best thing I perform.
line.ship_kostya.sat.1: Oh, you! You were tapping your foot yesterday. I saw. On the offbeat too, the right way. Who taught you? Nobody? Well, well.
line.ship_kostya.sun.1: Packing the kit today. Twenty minutes, nine cases. And unpacking again on Friday. A drummer's life: you carry more than you play.
line.ship_kostya.sun_day.1: We rehearse by day and I look out of the porthole. Blum says: "Kostya, the count!" But out there the sun's skipping on the water, one-and-two-and. That's what I count by.
line.ship_kostya.sun_night.1: After a concert my hands go on playing by themselves for an hour. I put them in my pockets and they tap away in there.
line.ship_lev.back.1: You're aboard again. I knew: the air felt somehow more cheerful on Friday.
line.ship_lev.first.1: Come in, but quietly: I'm listening. No, nothing is being sent. I'm listening to nothing being sent. That too is information.
line.ship_lev.morse.1: I hear Morse as speech. Every operator has a hand: one rattles, another draws out his dashes like vowels. I know the shore man by his first letter.
line.ship_lev.sat.1: Ah, yesterday's young man. Sit down. Shall I show you how your name sounds? There. Hear it? Now you exist on the air.
line.ship_lev.sun.1: I'm about to send to the shore: "On schedule, all well." The same every Sunday. The best telegram in the world.
line.ship_lev.sun_day.1: By day the air is noisy: the sun interferes with the short waves. It's a transmitter too, you know. Only nobody understands what it sends.
line.ship_lev.sun_night.1: At night you hear farther. Yesterday I picked up a ship off Spitsbergen. Her operator wished me good night. We've never met. It's the custom among us.
line.ship_lev.telegrams.1: Would you like to send a telegram? Five roubles. Advice is free: write shorter. On the air a spare word weighs like an anchor.
line.ship_lev.tg_done.1: One more word came from the shore for cabin twelve: "Cabbage". I don't decode other people's happiness. I only receive it.
line.ship_lev.tg_reply.2: "Both swallows." The grammar limps, the meaning is flawless. Sit down and listen to it go.
line.ship_lev.tg_reply.3: Dot, dash, dash, dot: that's P. Dot, dash: A. Hear it? "Papa" in Morse sounds like footsteps on a staircase.
line.ship_lev.tg_reply.4: Gone. In twenty minutes one angry man will go and start the dough. Have a postcard: with the compliments of the radio service.
line.ship_lev.tg_take.1: Young man, you're just who I need. You have young legs, and I have a telegram with no addressee.
line.ship_lev.tg_take.2: Listen: "Motor ship Polden. To Swallow. No longer angry. Expecting you both. Papa." That's all. No surname, no cabin.
line.ship_lev.tg_take.4: Forty years on the air, and I've only ever received swallows from the shore. Ask Nonna Arkadyevna: she has the list and a memory like a radar.
line.ship_lev.tg_wait.1: No Swallow yet? The telegram can wait, it doesn't eat. But there's a man at the other end not sleeping. I can hear that without headphones.
line.ship_lev.watch.1: I lost my watch to Albert, the engineer. He gave it back. He said: "A good watch ought to run with its owner." A handsome gesture. Too handsome.
line.ship_lev.years.1: Forty years on the air. In that time I've sent three thousand "I love you"s, two hundred "forgive me"s and one "send money, sinking". The last turned out to be a joke.
line.ship_misha.back.1: You again too? We've decided: we'll come every month. Olya says a honeymoon isn't obliged to end.
line.ship_misha.first.1: Hello. I'm Misha. My wife and I... my wife, fancy that... we're on our honeymoon. I'm a technologist. Fish. You don't want to hear about that.
line.ship_misha.fish.1: I know everything about sprats. Forty-one operations from the net to the tin. I told Olya that on our first date. She married me anyway.
line.ship_misha.olya.1: Olya's beautiful, isn't she? Sometimes I look and think: it's a mistake in the waybill. Any minute they'll come and say the goods aren't mine.
line.ship_misha.ring.1: I keep turning my ring. Not used to it. It's like a nut you're afraid to overtighten.
line.ship_misha.sat.1: Hi. Listen, did you see me break a cup at dinner yesterday? Everyone did. Olya said it's for luck. She says that about everything I drop.
line.ship_misha.sea.1: I've worked by the sea eight years and this is my first time on it. From the shore it's raw material. From here it's just the sea.
line.ship_misha.sun.1: Back today. To the cannery on Monday. I was afraid two days wasn't much. It turns out two days is a great deal, if you don't drop anything.
line.ship_misha.sun_low.1: Olya says: look, the sunset. I look at Olya. She says: not there. And I reckon, yes, there.
line.ship_misha.sun_night.1: At night Olya sleeps and I lie listening to her breathe. And the diesel. They have almost the same rhythm. It calms me.
line.ship_misha.waltz_confess.1: Did Olya send you? Don't answer. Even if she didn't, she soon will.
line.ship_misha.waltz_confess.2: I can't dance. At all. At the wedding I got away with it: the band was late, everyone just ate. But Saturday is a waltz in front of the captain.
line.ship_misha.waltz_confess.3: She danced at college. I saw her, and that's why I went up to meet her. And that's why I'm standing here now.
line.ship_misha.waltz_confess.4: Listen. There's a pianist in the saloon, grey-haired. Find out what they play first. Maybe it's not a waltz at least.
line.ship_misha.waltz_done_m.1: I didn't fall. Did you see? I didn't fall! Up to three. I'll count to three for the rest of my life.
line.ship_misha.waltz_done_m.3: You're lying. But thanks. Have some sweets, they're from the wedding table. We're still eating them.
line.ship_misha.waltz_done_m2.1: Olya says I count in my sleep. One, two, three. She says it's good to fall asleep to.
line.ship_misha.waltz_drill.1: One, two, three. One, two, three. Don't put me off. I've been round the lifeboat forty times. I think the lifeboat can do it by now.
line.ship_misha.waltz_lesson.2: Up to three. And I was counting to four. What a fool... Wait, show me. One. Two. Three, stand.
line.ship_misha.waltz_lesson.3: Is it working? How does it look? Honestly.
line.ship_misha.waltz_lesson.5: Then it's working. Come to the saloon on Saturday. If I fall, at least someone can say it looked good.
line.ship_misha.waltz_pace.1: Found out? Not yet? I'll go on standing. I'm good at standing, that I can do.
line.ship_nonna.back.1: With us again? I knew it. I didn't put anyone else down for your nail.
line.ship_nonna.cap_done.1: He gave you the binoculars? His own? Hm. He never let even me hold them. Take care of them. And comb your hair: with binoculars like that you can't go about any old how.
line.ship_nonna.cap_hint.1: The captain doesn't invite twice. He invites once and then remembers.
line.ship_nonna.cap_invite.1: You got the note? "May drop in" and "invited" are different things, remember it all your life.
line.ship_nonna.cap_invite.2: Arseny Pavlovich said: "That young man you keep reporting to me about." I do not keep reporting. I report to the point.
line.ship_nonna.cap_invite.3: The bridge is at the very top. The captain has the watch from eight to twelve and from four to seven. Comb your hair.
line.ship_nonna.captain.1: Arseny Pavlovich thinks he commands this ship. Let him. It's more convenient for me.
line.ship_nonna.first.1: Good day. Your cabin is on your ticket, the key is in your hand, dinner is at half past seven. Ask me the rest, I know it.
line.ship_nonna.first.3: Everything in the passenger list, and a little beyond. For instance, that you haven't had lunch.
line.ship_nonna.list.1: Forty-two passengers. I remember who isn't speaking to whom, and whom to seat with whom so that they do.
line.ship_nonna.lost.1: Each voyage they lose six umbrellas, two sets of false teeth and one wedding ring. The ring always turns up. The teeth don't.
line.ship_nonna.programme.1: The programme's on the board. But if you want to know what will actually happen, ask me.
line.ship_nonna.sat.1: Yesterday you sat alone. Today three people nod to you. By Sunday you'll know everyone by name. I see it every voyage and it pleases me every voyage.
line.ship_nonna.sharp_heard.1: I have been told about the engineer from Riga. There was no scene. There was a list. One pity: he's the best talker at the captain's table.
line.ship_nonna.sharp_knit.1: Givi whispered that I should sit by the card table with my knitting. I don't know why. But nobody won more than a rouble all evening.
line.ship_nonna.sun.1: You hand your key in to me at the gangway. And don't pull that face: I'll hang it on the same nail. The nail will wait.
line.ship_nonna.sun_cloudy.1: In dull weather there's a queue at my desk: everyone suddenly remembers what they meant to ask. The sun saves me half a day.
line.ship_nonna.sun_low.1: At sunset everyone goes to the starboard side and the ship lists half a degree. The captain pretends it was planned.
line.ship_nonna.sun_night.1: Lights out after eleven. I'm no watchman, but I know who isn't asleep. At this moment, for instance, you.
line.ship_nonna.tg_ask.1: To Swallow? From Papa? "You both"... So. Both means she isn't alone. So not Vera Ignatyevna and not Inga.
line.ship_nonna.tg_ask.2: The honeymooners, cabin twelve. Olya signed the list with her maiden name, crossed it out and wrote the new one. Her hand shook. I notice such things.
line.ship_nonna.tg_ask.3: Go to her yourself. If I come, it's an institution. You're just a boy with a telegram.
line.ship_nonna.tg_hint.1: Cabin twelve, promenade deck. At meals she's in the dining saloon, by the rail when there's an island, in the evening in the saloon. Don't dawdle: telegrams go sour faster than milk.
line.ship_olya.back.1: Oh, you're here too! We come every month now. I told Misha a honeymoon isn't obliged to end. He wrote it down.
line.ship_olya.cabin.1: We have cabin twelve. The window faces the sunset. Nonna Arkadyevna said it was chance. Nothing is ever chance with her.
line.ship_olya.dance.1: I danced at college. Waltz, polka, mazurka. I got a four for the mazurka and a five for patience.
line.ship_olya.dress.1: The dress is blue, with a white collar. Mum sewed it at nights. Papa pretended not to see and brought her tea.
line.ship_olya.first.1: Have you seen my husband? Tall, grey jacket, red ears. He's been "getting some air" aft for two hours.
line.ship_olya.first.2: Saturday is the captain's dinner and dancing. I brought my dress in a suitcase of its own. And he has "things to do". If you see him, ask what. Only don't say I sent you.
line.ship_olya.misha.1: On our first date Misha talked about sprats for an hour. Forty-one operations. I listened and thought: here's a man who won't leave anything out.
line.ship_olya.sat.1: Good morning! You know it's the captain's dinner tonight? I've known since six this morning. I've been ironing since six this morning.
line.ship_olya.sun.1: I don't want to go ashore. It'll all begin at once there: saucepans, queues, Monday. Here we're still bride and groom. Till six, at least.
line.ship_olya.sun_day.1: What a sun! I never noticed it in town. There it's between the houses, a piece at a time. Here it's whole, and all ours.
line.ship_olya.sun_low.1: I say to Misha: look, the sunset. And he looks at me. I get cross. But not very.
line.ship_olya.tg_done.1: Papa answered. One word: "Cabbage". He means the pie. In our family that's how you say "I love you".
line.ship_olya.tg_found.3: We married without him. He shouted: a sailor, over his dead body. And Misha isn't even a sailor, he's a technologist at the fish cannery.
line.ship_olya.tg_found.4: Take the operator an answer. Can you remember it? "Papa. Back on Sunday. Bake the pie. Both your swallows." Yes, "both". He'll understand.
line.ship_olya.tg_hurry.1: Still here? Run to the radio room before I change my mind and add three more pages.
line.ship_olya.waltz_after.1: Did you see? Did you see him counting? With his lips. One-two-three. The whole waltz.
line.ship_olya.waltz_after.2: He trod on my foot four times. It was the best waltz of my life, and at college I danced with soloists.
line.ship_olya.waltz_after.3: It was you who taught him, wasn't it? Hush. I know nothing. I'm clever.
line.ship_olya.waltz_before.1: He vanished for half a day and came back cheerful. I ask nothing. I'm clever. The dancing is on Saturday from half past eight.
line.ship_olya.waltz_wait.1: Mine's aft again, where they smoke. He doesn't smoke. He stands there. What business aft does a man have on his honeymoon?
line.ship_otar.back.1: You. Left of the stage. I remember.
line.ship_otar.carry.1: I carry him up the ladders myself. Eleven years. He's heavier than he looks. Like everything that stands at the bottom.
line.ship_otar.first.1: Otar. Double bass. Don't touch, he's asleep.
line.ship_otar.givi.1: Givi is my cousin. He talks for two. So I keep quiet.
line.ship_otar.low.1: Nobody hears the double bass. But take it away and everyone asks where the music went.
line.ship_otar.sat.1: Yesterday you stood to the left of the stage. That's where I'm heard best. By chance, I suppose. But thank you.
line.ship_otar.sea.1: The ship hums on one note. D. I tune to her.
line.ship_otar.spanner_drum.1: Looking for the twenty-seven spanner? Kostya has it. He tightens his drum with it and says the sound gets rounder. The sound is the same.
line.ship_otar.sun.1: We're in at six. I carry him off last. We're in no hurry.
line.ship_otar.sun_low.1: Sunset. A low note. A long one.
line.ship_otar.sun_night.1: At night you can hear him humming by himself in his case. From the engine. I don't interfere.
line.ship_pasha.back.1: You're back! And thin again. What do they feed you ashore, air? Sit down, I'll be right with you.
line.ship_pasha.borscht.1: Borscht for forty-two isn't borscht, it's a hydraulic engineering work. A bucket of beetroot alone.
line.ship_pasha.cat_done.1: One fish short again. I put it down as "loss in handling". My loss in handling is grey and purrs.
line.ship_pasha.cat_milk.1: Buying milk at the buffet? For science? I know that science: grey, with a torn ear.
line.ship_pasha.cat_milk.2: Tell her to keep out of my galley. My fish are counted, and she can't count.
line.ship_pasha.diesel_rag.1: A rag for Grandad? A white one? He's taking his diesel's temperature again.
line.ship_pasha.diesel_rag.2: Here, a handkerchief. Linen, ironed. No rag: he'd wipe with a rag and throw it out, but a handkerchief he'll bring back. Estonian. And tell him to come and eat, I've warmed his soup three times.
line.ship_pasha.diesel_soup.1: Did you give him the handkerchief? And tell him about the soup? You're all the same. The engine knocks, and nobody hears that a man hasn't eaten.
line.ship_pasha.first.1: What are you standing in the door for? Hungry? I can see by your eyes you are. Dinner's by the timetable, but a pie's outside the timetable. Here.
line.ship_pasha.potatoes.1: Want to help? Peeling potatoes. Fifteen minutes, then a pie and everything I know about this ship. And I've known her since fifty-nine.
line.ship_pasha.rolling.1: When she rolls the pans go sliding. I lash them down like the bosun lashes his boats. He got his knots from watching me, only he won't own up.
line.ship_pasha.sat.1: Yesterday you left your porridge. Today you finished it. So you've settled in. People take to my porridge on the second day, I've timed it.
line.ship_pasha.sun.1: You'll take pies for the road. Don't argue. It's a long way home from the pier, and who's going to feed you ashore?
line.ship_pasha.sun_day.1: The galley has one porthole, and that shines on the stove. I go by it: sun on the saucepan, time to salt.
line.ship_pasha.sun_low.1: For forty years I've seen the sunset as stewed fruit: pink, with red in it, and no stirring it with a spoon.
line.ship_pasha.thin.1: You're thin. All passengers are thin. They live on sandwiches ashore, then come to me for fattening. Never mind, two days will put it right.
line.ship_rimma.back.1: Look who it is! My forty-first! No, this time you'll be the first. First down on the list, first to be called on.
line.ship_rimma.before.1: I used to work at a house of culture, with the choir. Thirty people, all singing flat. Here there are forty-two and only Givi sings. A rest cure.
line.ship_rimma.first.1: Attention! New passenger sighted! Exercises at seven fifteen, games at half past eleven, dancing on Saturday. Refusals are not accepted; lateness is.
line.ship_rimma.games_award.1: Ship's boy! Rings: done. Shuffleboard: done. I present, before everyone... Nobody here? I present before the sea. Sea, attention: a certificate!
line.ship_rimma.games_award.2: Forty-two. Plan fulfilled. Know who the forty-second is? Me. Every voyage I write myself in last if I'm one short. Today I wasn't.
line.ship_rimma.games_award.3: The big diploma, the one with the gold disc, goes on Sunday to those with every stamp in their cruise card. But that's not joy, that's persistence. Nonna Arkadyevna is in charge of that.
line.ship_rimma.games_enroll.1: Right! Young, handsome, idle. I'm writing you down. Surname? Never mind, I'll put "ship's boy".
line.ship_rimma.games_enroll.2: The deck biathlon: ring toss aft and shuffleboard on the boat deck. The winner gets a certificate with the captain's seal. A real seal, I stamp it myself.
line.ship_rimma.games_enroll.3: And don't look at me like that. I have a plan for joy: forty-two people a voyage. You're the forty-first.
line.ship_rimma.games_wait.1: Rings aft, shuffleboard up top. You can play any time, but on Saturday from half past eleven I also blow the whistle.
line.ship_rimma.plan.1: You think it's easy to cheer people up? They resist! I have to chase them. I do about eight kilometres of deck a day.
line.ship_rimma.quiz.1: The quiz is on Sunday. A trick question: how many islands do we pass? Six! And everyone says five, because they slept through the Seal Rocks.
line.ship_rimma.sat.1: Ah, yesterday's silent one! You've quite a different face today. I'm noting it down: "Thawed." I have a column for that.
line.ship_rimma.sun.1: The last day. The hardest part of my job is Sunday after six. Everyone's gone, and I walk the deck blowing my whistle for nothing.
line.ship_rimma.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast. Never mind! For that I have lotto, charades and Givi with the story about his grandfather. The plan for joy does not recognise weather.
line.ship_rimma.sun_day.1: Sun! Everybody on deck! No, I mean it. By my figures a person in the sun smiles four minutes more per hour.
line.ship_rimma.sun_night.1: I'm on duty at night too. In case someone can't sleep and feels sad. Then I sit beside them and keep quiet. That's entertainment work as well, only you can't put it in the report.
line.ship_rimma.waltz_call.1: Tonight after the captain's dinner: the waltz! Those who can't will stand by the wall and envy. Those who can count to three already can.
line.ship_rimma.whistle.1: My whistle is a real referee's. I scatter gulls with it, gather passengers, and once stopped a fight over a deck chair.
line.ship_senya.back.1: You again! Hooray! Listen, it's all the same here, only there are forty-five steps now. Let's go and check!
line.ship_senya.captain.1: When I grow up I'll be a captain. Or a bosun. A bosun's louder. But the captain has binoculars.
line.ship_senya.count.1: I counted the steps. From our cabin to the very top it's forty-four. And forty-three going down. One of them goes somewhere.
line.ship_senya.first.1: Who are you? A passenger? I'm Senya. I'm ten. I know where everything on this ship is. Want me to show you where the anchor sleeps?
line.ship_senya.gull_thief.1: A gull stole my bublik! One with a spot on its beak! At the stern, right out of my hand. Granny said: "Your own fault, don't wave food about."
line.ship_senya.gulls.1: The gulls fight over bread like our class 3B over the ball. Only the gulls are fairer: at least they don't tell tales.
line.ship_senya.key_done.1: Granny opened the suitcase, looked at the shawl and shut it. She said: "All present." And she gave me the key again. I don't bury it now. I've written it down.
line.ship_senya.key_found.1: You found it! The green tape! Where was it?
line.ship_senya.key_found.3: That's it! I buried it as treasure so I wouldn't lose it. And forgot where. Pirates always do.
line.ship_senya.key_found.4: Here. A bit of glass from the Seal Rocks, a sailor gave it me. Green, like the tape. The most valuable thing I've got. Except Granny.
line.ship_senya.key_secret.1: Can you keep a secret? Properly, I mean. Not like grown-ups.
line.ship_senya.key_secret.2: I've lost the key of Granny's suitcase. She gave it me to hold. And the present for Mum is in there: a shawl, Granny knitted it for two years. Mum's meeting us on Sunday.
line.ship_senya.key_secret.3: I was playing pirates. I looked under the lifeboat cover. The deck chairs were an island. And under a bench on the deck below, where people walk, I had my treasure.
line.ship_senya.key_secret.4: The key's on a green tape. Find it, will you? I told Granny it's in my sock.
line.ship_senya.key_wait.1: Lifeboat, deck chairs, bench. Green tape. Granny's asked about the sock twice already. Shh, she's coming. We're talking about gulls.
line.ship_senya.sat.1: Hi! I saw you yesterday! You go about on your own too. Shall we go about together? I know where the engine door is and where the cat is. Oops. I mustn't say about the cat.
line.ship_senya.ship.1: It isn't a warship, it's a vessel. The bosun told me there's a difference. But I still say "warship" when he can't hear.
line.ship_senya.sun.1: Home today. Mum'll be on the pier. But I don't want it to end. Can you have both: Mum, and it not ending?
line.ship_senya.sun_day.1: Granny says: put your sun hat on. I say: sailors don't wear sun hats. She says: sailors wear what Granny tells them.
line.ship_senya.sun_low.1: Look, the sun's sinking! It'll hiss any second. It doesn't hiss. I listen every evening and it never hisses.
line.ship_senya.sun_night.1: I'm supposed to be in bed, but I got away. For five minutes. The ship's quite different at night: she breathes. Don't tell Granny.
line.ship_taras.back.1: Oho! An old acquaintance! Show me your hands. Better. Another ten voyages and I might trust you with a mooring line.
line.ship_taras.bell_leave.1: Chizh put in a word for you. After ten at night the bell is yours: one stroke, softly. Leave her alone by day, by day she tells the time. Strike two and you'll polish her all the way to port.
line.ship_taras.cat_after.1: She's drinking. Hear her lapping? Off you go. And remember: you saw nothing, I poured nothing.
line.ship_taras.cat_caught.1: Halt. What's in your pocket? Milk. And you're steering for the hatch.
line.ship_taras.cat_caught.2: Give it here. That's not how you pour for her: it goes in the lid of the can. She won't drink from a saucer, too proud.
line.ship_taras.cat_caught.4: I know every rivet of this ship, and this is a whole cat. Bosun's her name. Three years a stowaway, never buys a ticket.
line.ship_taras.cat_caught.5: She's got kittens down there, three. Tell nobody. Zoya least of all: she'll blab, and I'll have to put the cat ashore. Regulations.
line.ship_taras.cat_done.1: The grey one with the patch got out on deck yesterday. Nonna Arkadyevna pretended it was a gull. A good woman.
line.ship_taras.cat_hint.1: What are you creeping about for? Nobody walks the foredeck without business. With business, that's different. With milk from the buffet, say.
line.ship_taras.diesel_bosun.1: Grandad listening to his engine again? Then he remembers nothing. Not where his spanner is, not whether he's eaten. You see that he eats.
line.ship_taras.first.1: Oho! A new one! Show me your hands. Soft. Never mind, the sea has re-educated worse.
line.ship_taras.first.2: I'm Taras, the bosun. If something on deck is tied down, I tied it. If it's come loose, that wasn't me.
line.ship_taras.goat.1: Heard about the goat? No? And you won't. It happened. She ate the deck log. That's all, not another word.
line.ship_taras.knot.1: Want to see a knot? The bowline. King of knots: holds like death and comes undone with one finger. Like a good temper.
line.ship_taras.loud.1: I'm not shouting. That's just my voice, a deck voice. In the cabin I whisper. Mind, they hear that aft as well.
line.ship_taras.paint.1: A ship stands on her paint. No paint, and you get rust, and rust is the sea already come to call.
line.ship_taras.sat.1: Second day and you're rolling as you walk already. Your legs have worked it out. Your head will catch up.
line.ship_taras.sun.1: Ashore today. Don't you go moping there. The shore's all right too, if you know there's a sailing on Friday.
line.ship_taras.sun_cloudy.1: Murk. Ropes get heavy before rain, I know the weather by them before the operator does. Only don't tell him.
line.ship_taras.sun_day.1: Sun's high, the paint's drying. That's all I ask of it. Well, and that it's warm. Well, and that it looks nice.
line.ship_taras.sun_low.1: Look, the sun's going down right into the hawsepipe. I check every evening: it fits.
line.ship_vais.back.1: You again. The life jacket is under the berth. Yes, I know you know.
line.ship_vais.captain.1: The captain says "about nine knots". I say "eight point seven". Between us we run exactly to the timetable.
line.ship_vais.exact.1: Just now we are two cables from where we should be. I know in which direction. That is enough.
line.ship_vais.first.1: Chief Mate Vais. Your life jacket is in your cabin, under the berth. Check that it is there, not "probably there".
line.ship_vais.sat.1: You checked your life jacket three times yesterday. It was reported to me. You'll amount to something, unless you amount to an alarmist.
line.ship_vais.sleep.1: I sleep by day, from half past four. The night watch is mine. Someone has to look at the sea when nobody is looking at it.
line.ship_vais.stars.1: I fix our position by the stars. We have instruments too, but no star has ever asked me to change its battery.
line.ship_vais.sun.1: The last day. A hundred and ninety miles run, four minutes off the schedule. I do not forgive myself those four minutes.
line.ship_vais.sun_cloudy.1: Ten tenths cloud. No stars tonight. We go by dead reckoning: that is when you trust your own arithmetic.
line.ship_vais.sun_day.1: At noon we take the sun's altitude. Sextant, stopwatch, four minutes. The most honest four minutes of the day.
line.ship_vais.sun_night.1: See the three bright ones, high up? Vega, Deneb, Altair. As long as you can find them, you aren't lost.
line.ship_vais.watch_done.1: Someone struck the bell in the night. I did not enter it in the log. The log is for incidents, and that was not an incident.
line.ship_vais.watch_mate.1: Chizh has the wheel alone in the evenings. He thinks I am asleep. I am not: I lie and listen to how she runs. But he need not know that.
line.ship_vais.watch_mate.3: No. I shall show him. By not coming up.
line.ship_vera.back.1: Young man! Your second time too? Quite right. Material must be revised or it doesn't sink in.
line.ship_vera.first.1: Good day, young man. Are you at school? Then tell me quickly: which sea are we in? You don't know. Nobody does. Sit down, three out of five.
line.ship_vera.globe.1: When I retired they gave me a globe. With a light inside. I looked at it and bought a ticket for the ship.
line.ship_vera.library.1: There's a pilot book in the ship's library, have you read it? Every rock in it is written of with respect. If only people were written of like that.
line.ship_vera.map.1: All my life I stood with my back to the map and my face to the class. I ought to have done it the other way round, just once.
line.ship_vera.pilot_ask.1: Young man, are your eyes good? Mine were, before forty outline maps a week.
line.ship_vera.pilot_ask.2: Here's the list. Six islands. For thirty years I pointed at them on the wall and never saw one. I can't stand long at the rail: the wind.
line.ship_vera.pilot_ask.3: Stand there for me. Remember one thing about each island, one, but a real one. Tell me and I'll tick it. Three will do: three is already an archipelago.
line.ship_vera.pilot_done.1: I showed the captain my list. He said: "There's a mistake here: there are three Brothers, not two." For thirty years I taught children there were two.
line.ship_vera.pilot_hint.1: The bow or a bridge wing is the best place to look. And see the "Pilot" in the library: it says which island comes when, and on which side.
line.ship_vera.pilot_pencil.1: My pencil is a pupil's, Kolya Lapshin's. He used it to turn a two into a three in his report book. Now the pencil serves science.
line.ship_vera.pilot_tell.2: There. That's in no atlas: that they are smaller and farther. I used to say "scale" to the children, when I should have said "go and stand at the rail".
line.ship_vera.pilot_tell.3: Three ticks. The rest next voyage: I'm stubborn. And postcards for you. They've lain in my school atlas for a bookmark since fifty-eight.
line.ship_vera.pupils.1: I had twelve hundred pupils. Two became sailors. Both send postcards, and both write "pacific ocean" without capitals.
line.ship_vera.sat.1: Good morning, young man. I'm raising yesterday's three to a four: you said good morning first and didn't mix up the bow and the stern.
line.ship_vera.sun.1: Home today. I was afraid the real sea would be worse than the map. It turned out bigger. Bigger isn't worse or better. It's bigger.
line.ship_vera.sun_cloudy.1: Stratocumulus, base about a kilometre and a half. For forty years I haven't been able to just look at the sky. An occupational habit.
line.ship_vera.sun_day.1: The sun now stands exactly in the south. That is noon, young man, not what the clock says. Clocks were invented for lesson timetables.
line.ship_vera.sun_low.1: I used to explain to the children that the sun doesn't set, the Earth turns. Now I look and think: it sets. Forgive me, children.
line.ship_vera.tg_notme.1: A certain navigator called me Swallow in forty-nine. He sends no telegrams now. Look for someone younger, my dear.
line.ship_vitya.back.1: You again! Great. I'm not in my first season now, I'm in my first season and a week. Feel the difference?
line.ship_vitya.cap_waits.1: The captain was asking for you. He's on the bridge from eight till noon and from four till seven. Don't be scared, he only looks like an iceberg.
line.ship_vitya.captain.1: The captain calls me "sir", in a manner of speaking. Nobody in my life has spoken to me like that. It makes me stand straighter.
line.ship_vitya.compass.1: Look, the compass card floats in spirit. The bosun says they used to drink it. He's lying. Probably.
line.ship_vitya.first.1: Hi. Careful, this is the bridge. Passengers aren't really allowed, but stay, I'll say I didn't notice. I'm Vitya. Helmsman. First season.
line.ship_vitya.home.1: I'm from Lyudmilovsk, the Third Terrace. My mother still can't believe they took me on. She comes down to the promenade to watch us sail.
line.ship_vitya.sat.1: Oh, hi! Listen, I saw you from the bridge yesterday, standing aft. I see everyone now. From up here people are so small, and all ours.
line.ship_vitya.sun.1: We'll be in by six. Mum will be on the promenade, over there, by the third lamp. I can't sound the horn for her, but the captain always gives one short blast. For the gulls, he says.
line.ship_vitya.sun_low.1: Steering into the sunset is the hardest: the sun's right in the glass. The captain says: "Don't squint, Chizh, get used to it. That's it saying hello to you."
line.ship_vitya.sun_night.1: The wheelhouse is dark at night on purpose. So your eyes can see the sea. Scary at first, then you see it's more honest that way.
line.ship_vitya.watch_done.1: The bosun says the bell rings cleaner since you. He's making it up, of course. But I checked: it does.
line.ship_vitya.watch_fear.1: You're a passenger? Listen, do you sleep at night, or what?
line.ship_vitya.watch_fear.2: I'm at the wheel from half past six till midnight. From seven I'm alone: the captain's at dinner, Irina Sergeyevna sleeps before her own watch. First season.
line.ship_vitya.watch_fear.3: While it's light it's all right. But after ten they turn the deck lights down, and there's only black ahead. And it feels as if I'm the only one awake in the whole ship. Taking her nobody knows where.
line.ship_vitya.watch_fear.4: I'd like to know someone is standing in the bows. Not crew, just a person. Come out after ten and strike the bell, once, softly. I won't be able to turn round, but I'll be able to hear.
line.ship_vitya.watch_fear.5: Only don't touch it by day. By day the bosun will have your hands off for the bell. At night he's at cards.
line.ship_vitya.watch_tell.1: I heard it. One stroke. I looked out: there you were. I gave you a thumbs-up, did you see?
line.ship_vitya.watch_tell.2: Funny: nothing changed at all. Same water, same course. But my hands on the wheel went dry.
line.ship_vitya.watch_tell.3: Here. Chocolate. It's issued for the night watch, a bar a man. This one's yours: you stood a watch too.
line.ship_vitya.watch_wait.1: After ten. Once, softly. The bell is right in the bows, you can't miss it.
line.ship_vitya.watch_wait2.1: If tonight doesn't work, there's a night tomorrow too. And next voyage. I'll be here as well.
line.ship_vitya.wheel.1: You don't turn the wheel. You hold it. Turn it and the ship yaws, and the mate looks at you. She says nothing. She looks.
line.ship_zoya.back.1: Oh, it's you again! Two lumps, no lemon? I passed my test, by the way. A four. The beam held.
line.ship_zoya.cabins.1: You can tell everything about people from their cabins. Who left a book on the pillow, who hung socks on the porthole. I tell no one. Only Nonna Arkadyevna, and she knows anyway.
line.ship_zoya.cat_done.1: The little grey one got into the corridor yesterday. I put a tray over him and told the passengers it was soup cooling.
line.ship_zoya.cat_hear.1: Shh. Did you hear anything last night? From the bow, under the cargo hatch.
line.ship_zoya.cat_hear.3: Someone's crying. Thin, like that. Third voyage running. I won't go alone, I'm scared to open my shipping economics textbook alone.
line.ship_zoya.cat_hear.4: Go and listen, will you? The hatch on the bow, by the windlass. Not a word to the bosun: no animals aboard. There was an incident with a goat.
line.ship_zoya.cat_milk.2: A cat! Alive! She needs milk. There's some at the buffet hatch, in cartons. I'd give it you free, but I've a stock-take: pay for it and call it science.
line.ship_zoya.cat_milk_again.1: Did you take it? Careful past Taras. He stands on the foredeck from eight till twelve like a monument.
line.ship_zoya.cat_tell.1: Well? Did you find it? Who's there?
line.ship_zoya.cat_tell.3: From me?! I'm the one hiding it from him! I've been bringing her sausages since May!
line.ship_zoya.cat_tell.4: All right. Let him think I don't know. Here, sweets: for keeping quiet. We all keep quiet here.
line.ship_zoya.cat_wait.1: Well, did you listen? The hatch right at the bow. It's clearer at night, by day the winch creaks.
line.ship_zoya.first.1: Oh, good day, sir! I mean, hello. Tea with lemon or without? I'm Zoya. If you need anything in your cabin, that's me.
line.ship_zoya.future.1: When I qualify as an engineer I'll build ships. With wide corridors. So a stewardess with a tray and a passenger can pass without ballet.
line.ship_zoya.milk_window.1: Milk? In pyramids, at my hatch. Only don't say who it's for: I'll guess by myself and not sleep all night.
line.ship_zoya.sat.1: I put two lumps in your tea, the way you asked yesterday. See, I remembered. I can't remember my mechanics, but that I remember.
line.ship_zoya.study.1: I've a shipping economics test on Monday. Freight, tonnage, demurrage. Demurrage is what you pay for standing idle. I'm all demurrage myself: work and college.
line.ship_zoya.sun.1: On Sundays I always have a little cry when I strip the beds. Silly, isn't it? The cabins are empty and the pillows still warm.
line.ship_zoya.sun_day.1: By day there are sun discs in the corridor from the portholes, one for each cabin. I tell the time by them: when it reaches the seventh door, it's time to lay the tables.
line.ship_zoya.sun_night.1: You walk the corridor at night and behind every door someone's breathing. Forty-two people. I'm not scared, I just feel sort of responsible.
line.ship_zoya.tray.1: Know how to carry six glasses when she rolls? Don't look at them. Look at the glasses and you spill. Look ahead and you get there.
journal.heard.ship_taras_bell_leave: Taras the bosun has allowed me the bell: one stroke, after ten at night. For a second he promises a rag and polish.
journal.heard.ship_zoya_milk_window: Zoya told me herself where the milk is: at her buffet hatch, in pyramids. And asked me not to say who it's for. I didn't.
journal.heard.ship_vitya_cap_waits: Vitya says the captain has been asking for me. He is on the bridge from eight till noon and from four till seven. And he only looks like an iceberg.
journal.heard.ship_rimma_waltz_call: Rimma has announced a waltz after the captain's dinner. Whoever can count to three can dance, she says. Misha has been counting to three for half a day.
journal.heard.ship_otar_spanner_drum: Otar the bass player confirms it: the drummer has the twenty-seven spanner. Kostya tightens his drum with it "for a rounder sound".
journal.heard.ship_senya_gull_thief: Senya shouted across the whole deck that a gull with a spot on its beak stole his bublik at the stern. That is the very one Mori-san needs.
